lead: A `cd` in one Bash call is still in force in the next one, so a later `git status` or `grep` answers about the wrong directory instead of failing.
body: The tool keeps its working directory between calls even though shell state does not, so `cd website && npm run sync:rules` leaves every following call rooted in `website/`, where `git status --porcelain -- website` reports zero changes and a `grep -r` finds nothing. Prefix the next call with `cd /d/mwl &&`, or run the one-off as `cd <dir> && <cmd>` knowing the move sticks.
